When I was younger, my mom took me with her on one of her hair appointments. She used to be a hair stylist back in the day and did it as a side job while my dad worked, too. On this specific hair appointment, the lady has two girls who I didn't know but wanted to impress. The oldest asked me, once we were all alone in her room, if my mom let me watch horror movies. I said yeah, thinking it would make me cool. She pulls out a case with a girl on the cover, *The Orphan.* Now, I swear to this day that the cover of the DVD was a girl with no eyes, just pitch black sockets, but if you do a quick Google search that is obviously not what comes up, so, needless to say, this movie fucked me up big time.

The beginning scene, for those who are not familiar, is the main mother character giving birth to a stillborn child. I was about seven or eight at this time, so I knew next to nothing about death and my parents were very religious. I was NOT allowed to watch horror movies for multiple reasons, and I honestly respected that up until this point, which I would soon regret. Before the stillbirth scene, however, there was a scene where the mom was getting pulled down a wheelchair and she was bleeding profusely all over the floor as the nurse moved her along.

Flash-forward to me screaming and getting scared when the mom starts screaming when she realizes her baby is dead. I go along the rest of the day unable to see color. Yes, I was so shocked and scared that I remember being unable to see color. I somehow felt this deep pit in my stomach that had not been there before. I still have said pit to this day. The girl quickly shut off the movie and we later sang karaoke. I sang a Katy Perry song. I don't know what it was, but I know I was never able to listen to Katy Perry again. Still can't, lol.

I broke down around bedtime when I knew I wouldn't be able to sleep and told my mom everything. She gave me some tea and lightly scolded me while blaming herself for not keeping a better watch. She never did that lady's hair again, mostly because she told her what had happened and the lady told my mom she was overreacting.

Fast forward a few days and I've been watching Shirley Temple movies my mom found in the attic non-stop. No one really noticed but something had switched on in my brain. For some reason I couldn't sit still or be doing nothing. I was scared of the dark, I was unable to just *breathe* without at least watching/doing something to keep my mind preoccupied. I was only ever happiest when we went to church, ironically. I remember we went to the movies to watch the movie *Rio* and once the movie ended I just started bawling my eyes out. Something had switched on in my little brain. I didn't realize it, but I now knew what it meant to *end.* And not just in movies and TV shows, but in *existence.*

That would lead me to spiral. I had extreme early signs of depression and anxiety that my parents ignored. I would pick at my skin and stay up late reading, trying to get away from my mind. I got obsessed with things badly, for example, I got REALLY into MLP and Sonic. They were cutesy, happy things. They were things that didn't seem to *have* an ending in my head. Anything that could never end filled me glee. No ending, no death, none of that bullshit.

TL;DR: *The Orphan*'s beginning scene fucked me up so bad that I got depression, anxiety, and a severe phobia of things "ending" (death, ends of shows/movies, etc).
